evidence: 0113 (patient details on this facility's own lab and pharmacy work) is backward compatible, unsigned until the owner signs (reviewed_by is empty). Review reference: owner decision 25 of 2026-11-01 (D-Eminence, in chat), "all recommended except D5", on the Akos handover backend plan, item 3a (D8: emergency sessions see the patient details with the work); decision 23 of the same evening: labs and pharmacies run as stand-alone products for the whole facility. The plan's 0106 is now 0113 (coordinator's numbering of 3 Nov 2026); 0104-0112 belong to other work and are not on this branch; 0113 is written on 0103 (34d69557) and uses nothing they add. WHAT CHANGES. Two new functions, nothing else: lab.work_item_patient_cards(uuid[]) (md5 69b1836bb8d9493bdc0d6d7cc5e96515) and pharmacy.work_item_patient_cards(uuid[]) (md5 5a944e144033d04f86771a33ef41247b), plpgsql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, not STRICT, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp (every name qualified), owned by identity.patients' owner, no migration number in either body. Each answers, for the given work item ids, the patient's full_name, gender (as sex), dob and the last 4 characters of hid_code (the route card's columns, ehr.order_route_patient_card) only for a work item that is own work (order_route_id null), at the session's facility, whose member holds lab.work-item.read or pharmacy.work-item.read there (auth.membership_has_permission) and passes identity.has_active_consent_grant(patient, subject, membership, facility, 'read_records', the session's purpose), the own-row branch of the work items' read policy, so an emergency session with an active break-glass grant is included and a revoked, expired or held grant, a deny directive, an inactive membership or a disabled account gives no row. At most 200 ids, else 22023 WORK_ITEM_PATIENT_CARDS_INVALID. No table, column, index, constraint, policy, trigger, role or existing function changes; C12/C18 (pinned by 0090/0091) are untouched; no row is touched. runtime-grants.sql gains a 0113 block: EXECUTE on the Lab function to hid_lab_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, on the Pharmacy function to hid_pharmacy_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, both revoked from PUBLIC; the migration grants exactly the same. SERVICES: nothing calls the functions until lab-api and pharmacy-api images of this release run with OWN_WORK_PATIENT_CARD_ENABLED=true (new setting in each, off by default; the infrastructure sets no value). Off, they send no new statement and answer and audit exactly as before (jest). On, GET /lab/work-items, /lab/work-items/:id, /pharmacy/work-items and /pharmacy/work-items/:id add the existing optional patient to own rows, read in a savepoint (a failure leaves the rows without one), and each list writes one lab.work-item.list or pharmacy.work-item.list audit row per patient shown (basis consent, work item ids only), which the patient's access log (0093) shows as a view. Today's images on the new schema answer as before. PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): 0001-0103 applied (0103's identity.organization_application_admin_account body md5 186eb4ca420749b8bdb324bdc843bc50 the marker, and the three tables read); not applied yet (neither function exists); md5 of identity.has_active_consent_grant 8b12ce866ee75cce411a2721795ffb92, identity.has_active_membership bb52953ef1cd08527db61230a671859e, auth.membership_has_permission 65e3eaff93fe729fd5c5b986b80c9dd6, platform.current_actor_subject cf14c2d4a16d44a79ea9dbef9dc79c2b, current_facility_id c4a7c2989e83d9cedbf1f7b785a5aaed, current_membership_id 641989704fea95f885fbc38c6feb5aa5, current_purpose_of_use 74f7f2ea17dbbe825f7cfe543ad3e83f, lab.work_item_allows and pharmacy.work_item_allows b710e0c6b66ce87c8c4a059ad435b774 (identical bodies, so their search_paths, SECURITY DEFINER and STABLE too) and ehr.order_route_allows b80c2df6c380f7c7e20d166da94e56d2; the two work items' read policies (the only SELECT policies), work_items_route_facility_ck on both, forced row-level security on both and identity.patients' row-level security on and not forced; the types and NOT NULLs of the 13 columns read; the applier is identity.patients' owner or a member that inherits it and may SET ROLE to it, and may create in schemas lab and pharmacy; that owner may create in and use them, use identity, auth and platform, read identity.patients, lab.work_items and pharmacy.work_items and execute the eight functions the body and the read policies call. Negative copies on a 0103 base each stopped with nothing applied: the marker renamed and the marker body changed (0001-0103 must be applied first), a pinned body changed, pharmacy.work_item_allows' search_path changed, the consent test made SECURITY INVOKER, an extra read policy, a read policy changed, work_items_route_facility_ck dropped, FORCE lifted on lab.work_items, FORCE set on identity.patients, identity.patients.full_name made nullable, identity.patients owned by a role without the privileges (42501 listing each), a stranger with every schema's USAGE (42501, not the owner and may not act as it); a second apply answers 0113: already applied. LOCKS, measured with pg_locks before commit on a 0103 copy: ACCESS SHARE on schemas lab and pharmacy, the language plpgsql and the three granted roles, SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on the two new functions (their comments), ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the session's own temporary schema; no application table lock held to commit. Behind ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on lab.work_items the runner's dry run stopped after its 5 s lock timeout (5.2 s), nothing applied; behind ROW EXCLUSIVE on pharmacy.work_items, or ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on identity.patients, it ran in 0.2 s. Apply time 25 ms (execution_ms). PROVED on throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15: an upgrade of a 0001-0103 database with staging's runtime-grants.sql (sha256 594d7835...) by the runner: plan 1 pending, the dry run rolled back (104 recorded), apply, 0 pending, the file again answers 0113: already applied; the migration's grants equal this runtime-grants.sql's before and after the role bootstrap; bootstrap and role verification passed; all 78 database suites passed (16 in database/tests, 62 in test/database). A fresh install of all 105 files: plan 105 pending, dry run rolled back, applied, bootstrap and verification passed, 0 pending, all 78 suites passed. The staging schema upgrade rehearsal (db:test-staging-upgrade, NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator): passed, baseline 104, integrated 105, declared 0113_work_item_patient_cards.sql, dry run rolled back, applied checksums preserved, migration grants match runtime-grants.sql (2465 privileges), clean install, row-level security unchanged (185 tables). A database built by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner: 0113 applied by a member login of that owner (INHERIT and SET; the functions then belong to the owner), and the new suite and the pharmacy-prescription-source, pharmacy-dispensing-source, order-routes-receive and order-routes-privileges suites passed with that owner, so the functions read the work items through their forced read policies. The new suite fails on 0103. 15 of 17 mutants killed (no own-row filter, no consent test, write consent, no permission check, the Lab permission for Pharmacy, no 200 limit, a null list accepted, direct-care only, a 6-character ending, first name as sex, extra or PUBLIC EXECUTE); the two survivors drop the facility filter, which the permission and consent tests already imply (a membership belongs to one facility), kept as defence in depth. lab-api jest 486 and pharmacy-api jest 223 (including the off path, the savepoint failure, the per-patient audit rows and the injected setting) and both typechecks passed. The release contract needs every prefix up to the last, so npm --prefix release run verify and 3 of 98 release tests fail on the missing 0104-0112 only until they land or the coordinator renumbers; with placeholders for them the contract and those tests pass. SUITE: services/ehr-api/test/database/work-item-patient-cards.integration.sql: structure (bodies by md5, attributes, owner, EXECUTE exactly for each runtime, its API login and the schema test runtime); a member with read grants gets exactly its own rows' patients, identical to its own rows under row-level security, never a routed row it can read by consent, a patient without a grant or another facility's own work; nothing for a receptionist (consent, no read permission), a pharmacist through the Lab function and a laboratory scientist through the Pharmacy one, a session at another facility, without a membership, with an unknown subject or without a purpose, a revoked or expired grant and a disabled account; emergency: a break-glass grant under purpose emergency gets exactly its readable rows, nothing under direct care; 200 ids read, 201 and null refused 22023, an empty list answers nothing; no audit row written by the reads; the services' per-patient rows show in the patient's access log as views by the member at the facility.
